intended_object: For a graded ring A = ⨁ 𝒜ᵢ (ℕ-graded) and a point x of Proj A, which is a homogeneous prime 𝔭, this is the canonical ring map from the stalk 𝒪_{Proj A, x} to the homogeneous localization A_(𝔭) (degree-zero fractions). It sends a germ to the value of the section at x. Inferred from the docstring and from how the file uses it: later in the file it is proved to be an isomorphism.
explanation:
The stalk is the colimit, over open neighbourhoods U of x, of the section rings 𝒪(U). The definition defines the map out of this colimit by the universal property, using the cocone whose legs are `openToLocalization U x`, i.e. evaluation of a section at x. This is exactly the standard map that sends a germ to its value in the fibre. The lemma `stalkToFiberRingHom_germ` confirms it: the germ of s maps to s.1 ⟨x, hx⟩.

The file also constructs the inverse map `homogeneousLocalizationToStalk` and proves the two are inverse to each other, which gives the standard isomorphism of the stalk with A_(𝔭).

The generality is the right one: the Proj construction here is set up in the library for ℕ-graded rings, so the map cannot be stated more generally in this setting. I found no other Mathlib definition of this particular map. The analogue for Spec, `AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.stalkToFiberRingHom`, is a different object.
